samples.summary: Harness board mount omits `suppressSlideChrome: true`, so slide-scoped editor paths reach the newly-refusing store and throw
samples.evidence: The new board mount calls `S.initializeEditor({ canvas, overlay, store, hostWidth, hostHeight, dpr, viewport })` (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:537) over `asBoardStore(new S.MemSlidesStore(doc))`, which now throws for `addSlide`, `duplicateSlide`, `applyLayout`, the table ops, etc. The PRODUCT mount passes `suppressSlideChrome: true` precisely to keep those paths unreachable (packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:288, with the reason spelled out at :285-287). Without it: packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:529 (`Cmd+M` → `ctx.store.addSlide(...)` at :534), :556 (`Cmd+Shift+D` → `duplicateSlide`), :383/:353 (paste-source gating, incl. table paste) and packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:3421 (empty-canvas context menu keeps "Change layout…" → `applyLayout`) all execute against the board store. Any of those keystrokes/menu clicks — all reachable from the explorer, whose `key` action accepts any string (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs:151-152) — raises an uncaught `"…" is not supported on a board`, which the crash oracle turns into a candidate for a defect that does not exist in production. Fix belongs on the new mount: pass `suppressSlideChrome: true` (and, for parity, `cull: true`).

samples.summary: Grid snap is wired to toolbar state but never to the editor: `getSnapGrid` is not passed, so the snap the new charter tells hunters to expect is inert
samples.evidence: The board mount at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:537 omits the `getSnapGrid` option that the product mount supplies (packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:302-303 → `gridSnapRef.current ? gridStep(vp.current.zoom) : null`), and `SlidesEditor.activeSnapGrid` reads only `this.options.getSnapGrid?.() ?? null` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:6352-6354; option declared at :338, whose doc says omitting it makes every grid path unreachable). So toggling the harness's `gridSnap` state changes the toolbar label and nothing else — no drag is quantized and no grid is painted. Yet the new persona text states the opposite as measured fact: scripts/agent/charters-ui/board-author.md:79-83 ("THERE ARE TWO SNAPS… GRID SNAP, off in this harness by default and switchable from `Grid`. Both move a drag away from where you aimed") and the `arrange-and-view` brief in scripts/agent/charters-ui/personas.json ("the `Grid` menu has its own snap toggle… predict the snapped value"). A hunter following that either predicts snapped values that never occur or files "grid snap does nothing" — a harness-only artifact. Either pass `getSnapGrid`/`gridStep` through, or state in the charter that grid snap is state-only here.

samples.summary: New surface not registered in `SELECTION_READERS`, so every board action is keyed as selection shape `none` in the coverage memory
samples.evidence: `SELECTION_READERS` (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:88-93) lists `doc.selection`, `sheet.selectionRange`, `sheet.activeCell`, `slides.selection` — the new `board.selection` reader (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts, `"board.selection"`; advertised at scripts/agent/hunt-ui-tool.mjs board table) is absent. The module's own comment at :80-86 states the consequence: "A surface missing from here keys EVERY action as `none`, which is the state `sheet.activeCell` spent a year in and #847 fixed… a new surface has to be listed here as well as understood there." Every board run's coverage/pair memory will therefore record selection-less context for actions taken with elements selected. Searched: grep for `SELECTION_READERS`, `selectionShape`, `board.selection`, and all `slides.`/`doc.`/`sheet.` literals in scripts/agent/hunt-ui-coverage.mjs; no board registration anywhere in scripts/agent.

samples.summary: Charter states `Insert image` is "absent from the toolbar entirely"; the toolbar renders it (disabled) and the diff's own page comment says so
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/charters-ui/board-author.md:91 tells the explorer `Insert image` is absent from the toolbar. `BoardToolbar` in fact renders the button and only disables it when `onInsertImage` is missing (packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:349-358: `disabled={disabled || !editor || !onInsertImage}`), and the new page comment contradicts the charter directly: packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:739 — "`Insert sticky` and `Insert image` therefore render and do nothing". It happens not to show in `dom.controls` because disabled controls are filtered (packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-dom.mjs:43), but a hunter reading `dom.snapshot` will see a control the charter says does not exist.

samples.summary: Usage line still advertises only three surfaces after `board` was added
samples.evidence: docs/design/hunter-usage.md:91 documents `--surface <doc|sheet|slides>` while `UI_SURFACES` now includes `board` (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-surfaces.mjs:33) and the persona table two lines below already lists `board-author`/`board` (:106). Same stale enumeration exists in the CLI's own usage strings (scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:33 and :1743, `--surface doc|sheet`), which pre-date this change.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The harness board mount at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:537-545 calls S.initializeEditor with only {canvas, overlay, store, hostWidth, hostHeight, dpr, viewport} — no suppressSlideChrome (and no cull) — while the store is asBoardStore(new S.MemSlidesStore(doc)) (page.tsx:496), whose Proxy throws `YorkieBoardStore: "<m>" is not supported on a board` for the 34 listed methods (mem-board-store.ts:74-89, list at :26-61 incl. addSlide:29, applyLayout:31, duplicateSlide:35, table ops :33-38). The product mount does pass suppressSlideChrome: true with exactly this rationale (packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:284-288). The guards the option controls are real and are bypassed without it: keyboard.ts:529 (Cmd+M early-return, else store.addSlide at :534), keyboard.ts:556 (Cmd+Shift+D, else store.duplicateSlide at :557), keyboard.ts:353 and :383/:390 (table paste/duplicate filtering), and editor.ts:3421 (keeps "Change layout…", whose onPick calls store.applyLayout at :3435). Reachable: the editor registers its keydown handler on document in capture phase (editor.ts:2375), and the probe's `key` action accepts any non-empty string (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs:44,151-152). No caller-side guard or try/catch makes these unreachable in the harness, so this is a call site left inconsistent with the store contract other consumers satisfy — in-lane and blocking at major.

verdict.reason: The harness board mount at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:537-545 passes only canvas/overlay/store/hostWidth/hostHeight/dpr/viewport to S.initializeEditor — no getSnapGrid — and nothing else in the board branch (483-576) or elsewhere in packages/frontend/src/app/harness/ supplies or updates it (grep for /snap/i over that tree yields only the gridSnap state at page.tsx:401 and the props at 751-752, plus unrelated "snapshot" hits). SlidesEditor.activeSnapGrid derives the step exclusively from this.options.getSnapGrid?.() ?? null (editor.ts:6352-6357, option declared at :338), and initialize() injects no default (editor.ts:6743-6751), so every grid-snap path is unreachable in the harness. The toolbar is purely controlled: board-toolbar.tsx:233-238 renders the checkbox and calls onGridSnapChange, never touching the editor. The product mount does wire it (board-view.tsx:302-303, gridSnapRef.current ? gridStep(vp.current.zoom) : null), showing the harness is the outlier. Meanwhile the persona text asserts the snapped behaviour as fact: board-author.md:79-83 ("GRID SNAP … Both move a drag away from where you aimed … predict the snapped value") and personas.json:62 (arrange-and-view: "the `Grid` menu has its own snap toggle … predict the snapped value"). No charter line says grid snap is state-only for drags — board-author.md:94-95 only claims the controls are "wired to actual state", and personas.json:66 addresses a mode round trip, not drag quantization — so no counterexample exists. A hunter following the charter will either see predictions fail or file "grid snap does nothing", a harness-only artifact; the consumer left inconsistent with the documented contract is real and blocking.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `SELECTION_READERS` is defined once (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:88-93) with only doc.selection, sheet.selectionRange, sheet.activeCell, slides.selection, and is consumed at exactly one site via exact-match `.has(action.reader)` (line 257) — no prefix matching, alias table, or surface-derived registry anywhere in scripts/. The board surface is live on this branch (hunt-ui-surfaces.mjs:33 UI_SURFACES includes "board"; personas.json:50-52 defines a board-author persona) and its selection reader exists and is advertised to the model (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:78) and implemented (bridge.ts:518, returning an id array; oracle at verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:312). hunt-ui.mjs:1413-1418 passes the raw journal to coverageFromJournal with no reader renaming, so `shape` (initialised "none" at line 185, only updated in the line 257 branch) stays "none" for every board click keyed at line 296. `selectionShape` already handles the array shape (lines 131-134), so this is exactly the half-fix the module's own comment at lines 80-93 warns about, mirroring the slides registration proven necessary by the test at hunt-ui-coverage.test.mjs:46-59. Blast-radius lane: an existing consumer of the reader-name contract was not updated when the new surface was added; impact is a silently degraded coverage/pair memory for every board run, i.e. major, not critical (no data loss or guard bypass).
